statement: We introduce the first authorization-to-recovery lifecycle for AI agents.
justification: Prior academic, standards, and practitioner work already spans major portions of this lifecycle.

statement: Post-effect verification/recovery is a new concept introduced by this review.
justification: Execution-outcome verification and recovery are already explicit in prior work.

statement: Runtime governance of agent actions has not previously been studied.
justification: Runtime governance and authorization are established adjacent literatures.

statement: This review develops an evidence-mapped Decision-Validity Architecture that organizes heterogeneous controls by the locus at which validity must be established or restored.
justification: Supported by frozen v102 taxonomy and 13/13 CORE architecture coverage in v105.

statement: The review quantitatively distinguishes demonstrated CORE mechanisms from architectural/conceptual CORE_REVIEW proposals.
justification: 13 CORE versus 45 CORE_REVIEW, with explicit maturity and mechanism coding.

statement: The synthesis reveals an evidence gradient: demonstrated support is strongest around decision formation/validation and enforceable guardrails, while later lifecycle loci—especially post-effect closure—remain empirically sparse.
Protocol/governance architecture is more prevalent in CORE_REVIEW than CORE, whereas deterministic/policy guardrails are substantially more concentrated in CORE.
justification: Guardrails 7/13 CORE vs 6/45 CORE_REVIEW; Fisher p=0.00496. Trust/protocol governance 0/13 vs 12/45; sparse-cell caution.

statement: The framework proves that the five loci form a causal sequence.
justification: The architecture is evidence-derived and organizational; causal ordering has not been experimentally established.

statement: The identified gaps characterize all agentic AI research.
justification: Evidence is domain-concentrated: cybersecurity/network/cloud comprises 34/58 records.
